title: Infrastructure Keeps Going Down. I Found 5 Stocks Getting Paid
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names and figures in places
summary: Brian maps the cybersecurity patching wave after two weeks of outages — Microsoft down, the FAA grounding planes, Chase customers locked out of banking — which the top US intelligence official attributes to institutions patching software, not a coordinated attack. AI is finding vulnerabilities faster than anyone can fix them: Anthropic's Mythos, built in April, was so good at finding holes it was not released publicly, and Microsoft fixed over 1,400 holes in October alone, more than all of last year. Gartner expects cybersecurity spending up nearly 12% next year, though budgets have not grown yet. He covers eight names: Palo Alto Networks (~86x next-year earnings vs ~50x five-year average; XSIAM cuts response to under 10 minutes, sales up 39%); CrowdStrike (~148x; kept 97% of customers after the 2024 outage, margins swung from −46% to +22%, new AI-agent security product); Tenable (his most interesting name, PE ~18, AI scores only 1.6% of holes as real risk); Cognizant (~9x, bookings down 7%, Y2K comparison); Accenture (security $10bn, watch mid-December results); and Rapid7, Check Point and Fortinet, framed negatively as riding the wave without the business to back it. No explicit BUY/SELL/HOLD calls — all eight recorded UNCERTAIN; he says to watch earnings over the next two months and pick moments strategically.
